newsitem.title: JAPAN: New earthquakes jolt Japan resort.
newsitem.headline: New earthquakes jolt Japan resort.

text.p: A series of moderate earthquakes jolted a seaside resort near Tokyo on Friday in the latest series of earthquakes unnerving the region, the Meteorological Agency said.
The tremors temporarily halted trains in the area but caused no damage or injuries, police said.
The quakes measured up to five on the Japanese scale of seven, and 4.6 on the Richter scale.
Since Monday 6,350 tremors, including 247 strong enough to be felt by residents, have hit the city of Ito, on the coast of the Izu Peninsula 120 km (75 miles) southwest of Tokyo.
The strongest tremor, measuring 5.7 on the Richter scale, shook the area on Tuesday.
The agency has said the tremors, described as "swarm activity," all had shallow epicentres and pointed to undersea volcanic activity.

"Some people believe that the cyclical repetition of moderate eathquakes release stress in the earth so the chances of a big eruption are reduced. But it's not that simple and it can't be scientifically proven," an agency seismologist told Reuters.
Ito was shaken last October by an earthquake swarm of more than 5,000 tremors, but there was no damage.
Ito, a city of 72,000 people, is a popular resort and residents are suffering from a drop in tourism.
Ito officials said nearly 40,000 tourists have cancelled hotel reservations since the latest earthquake swarm started on Monday.
